title: The I2C Hardware Bus Scanner Sketch (Wire.h)
summary: Build and execute an industrial-grade diagnostic I2C bus scanner sketch to detect, verify, and map all active peripheral addresses.

steps.title: The Hardware Detective: The I2C Bus Scanner
steps.markdownContent:
### The Engineer's Golden Diagnostic Rule
Whenever you construct a multi-device embedded circuit on a breadboard, **never jump straight into uploading your complex final application code**!

Why? Because if a jumper wire is in the wrong breadboard hole, an address is mistyped in your sketch, or a sensor backpack is hardwired to an alternate address (like `0x3F` instead of `0x27`), your application code will freeze or silently fail. You will waste hours guessing whether the problem is a software bug, a burnt component, or a bad wire.

Professional robotics engineers always deploy a **Hardware Bus Scanner** first. Think of an I2C scanner like sonar sweeping across an ocean: it systematically pings every valid 7-bit address from `1` to `126` (`0x01` through `0x7E`).

```
I2C SCANNER RADAR SWEEP (Pinging 7-Bit Address Space):
Controller broadcasts: 0x01? -> No reply (NACK)
Controller broadcasts: 0x02? -> No reply (NACK)
...
Controller broadcasts: 0x27? -> [PULLS SDA LOW: ACK!] -> Device Discovered: 16x2 LCD!
...
Controller broadcasts: 0x57? -> [PULLS SDA LOW: ACK!] -> Device Discovered: AT24C32 EEPROM!
Controller broadcasts: 0x68? -> [PULLS SDA LOW: ACK!] -> Device Discovered: DS3231 RTC!
Sweep Complete: 3 Devices Discovered on Bus.
```

### The Mystery of the Third Device: Address 0x57!
When you scan your bus with both the LCD (`comp_07`) and DS3231 RTC (`comp_10`) connected, you might expect to see exactly two devices: `0x27` and `0x68`. But the scanner will frequently report **three devices**: `0x27`, `0x57`, and `0x68`!

Who is `0x57`? Look closely at your DS3231 breakout board: next to the clock chip sits a tiny 8-pin **AT24C32 EEPROM** non-volatile memory chip! The manufacturer included it so you can log sensor data offline. The scanner uncovers the hidden silicon automatically!

quickCheck.question: How does an I2C bus scanner sketch determine whether a device is physically present at a specific address?
options: It calls Wire.endTransmission() and checks if the return code is 0 (ACK bit received on clock pulse 9)
It reads the barcode sticker on the back of the module using an optical laser
It measures the temperature of the ATmega328P microcontroller
quickCheck.explanation: When the scanner addresses a device, a functioning peripheral pulls SDA LOW on the 9th clock pulse to send an ACK. Wire.endTransmission() returns 0 when this ACK is detected.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Recall the ACK/NACK handshake from Course 8: an ACK pulse (0) confirms a device heard its address.

quickCheck.question: Why does a DS3231 RTC breakout module often show TWO responding addresses (0x68 and 0x57) during an I2C bus scan?
options: The breakout board includes an onboard AT24C32 EEPROM memory chip at address 0x57 in addition to the DS3231 RTC at 0x68
The DS3231 clock is divided into morning and evening addresses
The Arduino Uno creates a duplicate mirror address to double clock speed
quickCheck.explanation: Most standard DS3231 breakout modules include an onboard AT24C32 I2C EEPROM chip at address 0x57 alongside the DS3231 RTC chip at address 0x68.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Many breakout boards package companion chips (like non-volatile EEPROM memory) onto the same PCB.

steps.title: The Anatomy of an I2C Address Ping & Return Codes
steps.markdownContent:
### The Transmission Cycle of a Scanner Ping

When `Wire.beginTransmission(address)` and `Wire.endTransmission()` execute, the ATmega328P hardware executes a complete bus probe:

```
SCL: ──┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐   ┌───┐
       │   │ 1 │   │ 2 │   │ 3 │   │ 4 │   │ 5 │   │ 6 │   │ 7 │   │ 8 │   │ 9 │ (ACK Clock)
       └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘   └───┘
SDA: ──┐   [Bit6]  [Bit5]  [Bit4]  [Bit3]  [Bit2]  [Bit1]  [Bit0]  [R/W=0] ┌─────── (Released by MCU)
       └─── (7-Bit Target Address: e.g. 0x27)                              └───▼─── (PULLED LOW BY TARGET!)
      START                                                                  ACK
```

### Wire.endTransmission() Return Codes:
- **`0` = Success (ACK Received):** The target recognized its address and pulled SDA LOW during clock cycle 9. A working device is present!
- **`1` = Data Too Long:** Data exceeded the internal 32-byte `Wire` buffer.
- **`2` = Address NACK (No Device):** Nobody pulled SDA LOW during clock cycle 9 (the line stayed passively HIGH). No device exists at this address.
- **`3` = Data NACK:** Device accepted its address but refused subsequent data bytes.
- **`4` = Other Error:** Bus arbitration lost, line held low by hardware fault, or SDA/SCL shorted to Ground or VCC.

### The 7-Bit Address Space Boundaries
Addresses `0x00` through `0x07` and `0x78` through `0x7F` are reserved by the official Philips/NXP I2C specification for special functions (general calls, 10-bit addressing, high-speed mode). The scanner safely sweeps **`0x01` through `0x7E`** (1 to 126 in decimal).

steps.markdownContent: Test your mastery of I2C bus scanner routines, status return codes, and address mapping.

interactiveConfig.question: What does a return value of 0 from Wire.endTransmission() signify during an address scan?
options: The addressed peripheral successfully pulled SDA LOW during the 9th clock cycle (ACK received)
The bus suffered a fatal short circuit to ground
The Arduino has run out of dynamic RAM memory
interactiveConfig.explanation: Return code 0 indicates success: the target device acknowledged its address by asserting an ACK on the 9th clock pulse.

questions.question: What does a return value of 0 from Wire.endTransmission() signify during an address scan?
options: The addressed peripheral successfully pulled SDA LOW during the 9th clock cycle (ACK received)
The bus suffered a fatal short circuit to ground
The Arduino has run out of dynamic RAM memory
questions.explanation: Return code 0 indicates success: the target device acknowledged its address by asserting an ACK on the 9th clock pulse.

questions.question: What does return code 2 from Wire.endTransmission() indicate when scanning address 0x40?
options: Address NACK: no device on the bus acknowledged address 0x40
The device at address 0x40 is transmitting streaming video
questions.explanation: Return code 2 indicates an Address NACK: no device recognized the address, so the SDA line remained passively pulled HIGH by the pull-up resistor.

questions.question: Why is running an I2C scanner the recommended first step whenever assembling a multi-device breadboard?
options: It isolates physical wiring, power, and addressing errors from high-level software application bugs
It uploads firmware into peripheral sensor microchips
It increases the USB voltage from 5V to 12V
questions.explanation: Running a scanner verifies physical electrical continuity, confirms power and ground rails, and proves the hardware addresses independently of complex application libraries.
